Hey again,

So the final answer is that if the account deletion request is clear, we should always delete the account, no questions asked. If it’s a ticket with the “Delete my account” title but has a hidden complaint in it (and the user does not say exactly “I want you to delete my account”), we solve the user’s complaint and ask if they still wish to delete the account. 

The ticket can be put on-hold and if the user does not get back to us confirming they do not want to delete the account, we proceed with their account deletion. We should also mention in our reply that if they don’t get back to us in 5 days (I think that’s the time the ticket will be on-hold before it changes to open again), we’ll delete their account.

I hope this clarified it. Let me know if you have any questions 🙂

Hey, sorry for the delay - after me being sick, our main POC at the external firm was OOO. Long story below but in short, liability arises if specific health and safety regulations have not been followed. I understand that appropriate means have been put to place by our Risk and Safety team but please do confirm to take the risk off here.

+++

Polish law imposes an obligation on employers to provide their employees with safe and hygienic working conditions. The employer's obligations in this respect are regulated both in the Polish Labour Code as well as in numerous ministerial decrees. It is the responsibility of the employer to ensure health and safety in the workplace (e.g. the employer's obligations include providing the employee with efficient and safe working tools).

Addressing the issue of criminal liability for the death of an employee, if the cause of the employee's death is the employer's failure to comply with health and safety regulations then the employer may incur criminal liability under Article 155 of the Polish Criminal Code. According to Article 155 of the Polish Criminal Code: „Anyone who unintentionally causes a person's death is liable to imprisonment for between three months and five years”.

On the other hand, if the employer's violation of health and safety regulations resulted in an employee's injury, the type of criminal liability depends on the type of employee’s injury. In the case of grievous bodily harm (and assuming the offender acts unintentionally) the offender is liable to imprisonment for up to three years (Article 156 § 2 of the Polish Criminal Code). In the case of a bodily injury or an impairment to health other than as specified in Article 156 § 1 of the Polish Criminal Code or a bodily injury or an impairment to health lasting up to seven days (and assuming the offender acts unintentionally) the offender is liable to a fine, the restriction of liberty or imprisonment for up to one year.

It should be noted that there must be a direct cause-and-effect link between the employer's violation of health and safety rules and regulations and the employee’s death or injury; in the case of an omission, in order for an effect to be attributed (and to impute criminal liability to the offender), it is necessary to establish that in the light of knowledge and life experience, taking an action that the perpetrator was obliged to take substantially increased the chance of preventing such an effect as occurred. 

Notwithstanding the foregoing, the employer  will not be criminally liable if he has complied with the health and safety rules and regulations and the accident was caused by the employee.

As I indicated above, it is the responsibility of the employer to provide safe working conditions. If the employer is a legal entity, then the person who is responsible for ensuring safe working conditions at the workplace will be held criminally liable. This may include, in particular, members of the management board and managers of employees (the managaer of employees may be for instance a foreman, manager of a department, division, branch, director; it is a person who has the authority to enforce compliance with health and safety regulations and rules by employees).

I must add that the persons described above may bear criminal liability not only when the death or injury of an employee occurs, but also if as a result of negligence in the duty to ensure safe working conditions, an employee is exposed to to an immediate danger of loss of life or serious injury. Pursuant to Article 220 § 1 of the Polish Criminal Code “Anyone who fails to perform his or her responsibilities concerning occupational health and safety, and thereby exposes an employee to an immediate danger of loss of life or serious injury, is liable to imprisonment for up to three years”. According to Article 220 § 2 of the Polish Criminal Code “If the offender acts unintentionally, he or she is liable to a fine, the restriction of liberty or imprisonment for up to one year”.

Hey [~accountid:617baa2a327da40069521341], received response from the law firm. In short, our app needs to have a feature of client identification before purchasing the alcohol. We are currently not compliant with that requirement. We will analyze whether there are any workarounds or whether the only way to comply is to make amendments to the product.

----

# _We understand that the point of sale in case of alcohol sales is considered the webpage / mobile phone application. Does this rule apply to Bolt Food as well? For background, our T&Cs outline that the sale agreement is only concluded between the restaurant / store and the customer. Bolt Food as an application only facilitates the sales and does not participate in the agreement between the customer and the restaurant / store._

Yes, in this case, the webpage / mobile phone application is considered the point of sale. You are also right that from a legal point of view the seller is restaurant and not Bolt Food. Accordingly, even if selling on Bolt Food platform, the restaurant is still obliged to verify customer’s age. Theoretically, if the restaurant cannot achieve it through own means, it should ask Bolt Food to implement measures that allow for age verification (the actual verification may be performed on restaurant’s behalf by Bolt or a third-party service provider), otherwise the restaurant is not allowed to perform distance sale of alcohol and risks an administrative fine up to 7100 € (and in case of repeated offences may lose the alcohol retail licence).

 

_2. We understand that in order to buy alcohol customers are required to identify themselves using AeS/QeS measures. On Bolt Food app the customer is obliged to confirm that he/she is at least 18 years old while purchasing alcohol, and upon delivery of the alcohol the ID of the customer is checked by the courier. Does Bolt Food currently comply with Latvian requirement to check the identity of our customer upon alcohol purchase?_

 

Customer’s age must be verified twice – online before making the purchase and also in-person at the time of delivery. So the second step (delivery) seems to be okay but first step (online) is not compliant. Pursuant to Article 6.^1^(4) of the Law on Handling Alcoholic Beverages, the buyer’s identity must be verified using either:

# means of electronic identification that correspond at least to level “qualified” or “qualified increased security”;^1^ or

 

# strong customer authentication within the meaning of Article 4(30) of Payment Services Directive 2 (directive (EU) 2015/2366).^2^

^_____________________________^

^1^ The functional requirements for obtaining each of these levels are provided in [Cabinet of Ministers regulations No 560|https://likumi.lv/ta/en/en/id/293654-regulations-regarding-the-technical-and-organisational-requirements-for-the-qualified-and-qualified-increased-security-electronic-identification-service-provider-and-the-service-provided-thereby], but even the less stringent level “qualified” requires two different authentication factors, so the current system where the customer simply confirms (e.g., by use of check-box) that he/she is 18 years old does not comply with Latvian requirements.

^*2*^ Used by most online banking apps and there are third party service providers who provide this service to others for a fee (allegedly ~ 0,50 € per verification). Apart from Smart-ID we have also heard the names of “Contumatic”, “Veriff” and “Zippyid”.

HI Sam, 

please find below an external counsel’s answer. 

Unfortunately, the legislation is not straightforward, but rather broad. Basically, there is no training _as such_ for First Aid officers, but instead, the law prescribes that it must be a person with knowledge (conditions are set in cooperation with the provider of labour health services) 

 Should you have any questions, please ask. 🙂 

“_Czech labour law states as follows:_

* _The law stipulates, under certain conditions, the obligation of employer (BOLT) to ensure the fulfilment of risk prevention tasks through a professionally qualified person._

* _Ensuring the provision of first aid is one of the basic obligations of the employer._

* _In the event of an emergency, the employer is obliged to provide and determine the required number of employees who organize the provision of first aid, ensure the summoning of the emergency medical service provider, the Fire and Rescue Service of the Czech Republic and the Police of the Czech Republic._

* _The employer is obliged to equip the workplace where employees work at night with the means for providing first aid, including the provision of means enabling emergency medical assistance to be called._

_The law stipulates in some cases the obligation to ensure risk prevention through a professionally qualified person (which will be similar to the First aid Officer you mentioned). The requirements for a professionally qualified person are then set by law._

* _In the case of a maximum of 25 employees, the employer may perform the risk prevention tasks himself if he has the necessary knowledge,_

* _in the case of 26 to 500 employees, the employer may provide risk prevention tasks himself, if he is professionally qualified, or by one or more professionally qualified persons,_

* _in the case of more than 500 employees, the employer always performs risk prevention tasks by one or more professionally qualified persons._

_The employer himself may be a professionally qualified person, but only if he is qualified to do so and if he meets the following conditions: if it employs a maximum of 25 staff and has the necessary knowledge to do so, if it employs 26 to 500 employees and is professionally qualified to do so._

_However, the employer may entrust this task to his employee, who, however, must meet the legally prescribed requirements and conditions. A professionally qualified person does not necessarily have to be an employee – the employer may outsource one or more professionally qualified persons._

_It is the employer's responsibility to ensure and determine the required number of employees who organize the provision of first aid, depending on the type of activity and the size of the workplace. The employer is obliged to ensure, in cooperation with the provider of labour health services, the training of these employees and equipment to the extent corresponding to the risks occurring at the workplace. As you can see, the law sets out these obligations in a relatively general way and it is therefore always necessary to address occupational safety individually according to the circumstances of a particular workplace. Therefore, I highly recommend hiring an occupational safety specialist to help you set up your occupational safety system exactly according to your needs and specific circumstances._

_For completeness, I also answer your questions as follows:_

* *_Is it necessary for the company to appoint and train a First Aid Officer in CZ?_*

_There is position of professionally qualified person in risk prevention tasks in Czech labour law. This position must be provided by the employer under the above conditions. The employer is also obliged to provide the necessary number of employees who are able to organize the provision of first aid._

* *_If yes, is there any threshold prescribed, meaning the number of employees of the company that triggers the obligatory appointment and training of the First Aid officer?_* 

_See thresholds above (for employer to have an obligation to provide professionally qualified person in risk prevention tasks). The organization of occupational safety, including the provision of first aid, also must be adequate to your operations and workplace conditions._

* *_Also, is there a specific first aid training course that needs to be completed in order for someone to be considered the site's First Aid Officer? If yes, can you please provide us with information on what such training must include?_*

_The labour law lays down specific conditions for professionally qualified persons in risk prevention tasks. These include education, professional experience, successfully passed a periodic professional exam, etc. Also your employees must be trained to an adequate extent of the risks involved in the workplace – nevertheless there are no specific training courses. You are obliged to provide this training in cooperation with your occupational health service provider. I also recommend consulting an occupational safety expert on this matter.”_

BR, 

Iva

Hey\!

So essentially we’re making a public offer to sign up for the use of Bolt Business (Team Account), and if the requirements we have set are met then the benefits (in the limits we have announced) can be enjoyed by the Customer.

These requirements and limits related to the offer (wherever and however we communicate this offer) need to be clear and comprehensive up front. Meaning, we can’t add further prerequisites or limits later on (we can ofc repeat these in any subsequent comms, e.g in the activation email but these shouldn’t introduce anything new in that regard). 

These conditions do not have to be provided as a separate T&C document or whatnot (unless they are so lengthy that it just makes sense to do so) but can instead be included in the comms text itself if a reasonable compromise can be found between marketing copywriting and legal precision. 🙂 

From what I understand from the materials you provided we do not limit the persons who can sign up in any manner as long as the person enters the data requested within the sign-up funnel. Meaning, even if we direct a particular campaign to, say' Swedish market, also a Georgian registered Customer can sign up and benefit from the campaign should it somehow become aware of the campaign?

Based on the input I understand the limitations below apply, hence these should be included in the comms respectively. Should any part of the limitations be overly lengthy, e.g the discount cap per market then this can be incorporated by reference (e.g as a table), see e.g the below:

_Sign up for \[Bolt Business/ Team Account], use the promo code \[promo code name], and get a \[50/75]% discount for up to 50 rides*. The total value of discounted rides is limited per market* as \[provided here/ follows]:_
_The promo code is valid until \[04.05.2022] for a travel period of one month since receiving the discount activation email from Bolt._

*”Rides” can lingually refer to all - ride-hailing, e-vehicle and car-sharing trips, so should this need to be limited in any way then let’s do so.
**Without further elaboration ”limited per market” however refers that a Customer can still at leats theoretically go beyond the listed thresholds if its Users ride in different markets.

Do let me know in case of further specifications or questions\! 

As said, the exact wording is flexible to some extent. Also some bits and pieces might not be relevant to be repeated at some stage of comms, e.g no need to add “Sign up to …” in an activation email when the Customer has already signed up.

Cheers,

A.

So let’s check the period 10 - 17 April (where he received a payout of 20.8 azn on the 17th). We can see the balance is positive prior to the period: 8.19 azn - this is the extra sum he’s manually transferred to his balance:

!Screenshot 2022-04-21 at 16.50.01.png|width=1176,height=216!

When summarising all the cash orders he’s taken (external type = cashPayment) the sum for the week is -694.89 azn → this is the amount cash they received during the week

When summarising all the cash payments he’s done (external type = payment) the sum for the week is 707.5 azn → this is the amount cash they’ve sent to Bolt, which is > the cashPayment sum. 

Putting all the information above together:

8.19 + 707.5 - 694.89 = 20.8 azn which is equal to the payout amount (& this represents the extra cash on his courier balance). Remember cash is the responsibility of the courier (not fleet) hence we have no way to ‘send’ this extra balance to the fleet account & that’s why it was paid out on the 17th.

*Sunday ban* - risks for any kind of workaround are too high

# Sunday ban - the authority that issued the permit for the sale of alcoholic beverages shall revoke the permit in the event that the entrepreneur violates the terms and conditions of the sale of alcoholic beverages and also the company can be subject to a fine of PLN 1 000 to 100 000 and the responsible person shall be liable to a fine (from PLN 100 to PLN 1 080 000) or to a penalty of restriction of liberty (Article 228a of Polish Criminal Code)

*Additional requirements* 

regarding *the T&Cs* these are the obligations : some entrepreneurs who deliver alcohol to customers through couriers include in their T&C provisions according to which:

* the place of sale is the physical point of sale (vide Article 9(6) of the Act on Upbringing in Sobriety and Counteracting Alcoholism) specified if their permit;
* the customer may collect the alcohol in person from the point of sale or the alcohol may be delivered to customer by a courier 

*authorised by him* (when placing an order online and selecting delivery, the customer checks the box that he authorizes the courier to pick up the order on his behalf - in the seller’s opinion the goods are released to the customer at the moment when the seller releases the ordered goods to the courier, therefore the sale is conducted at the point of sale and not at the place of delivery; this position was disagreed with, among others, by the Administrative Court in Warsaw in a judgment dated 12 April 2019, VI SA/Wa 1688/18).Apart from displaying the information on harmful effects of the consumption of alcohol, you need to know that according to Article 15.1. of the Act on Upbringing in Sobriety and Counteracting Alcoholism, selling alcohol to intoxicated persons and to minors is prohibited. Therefore, your T&C should clearly repeat that it is not possible to purchase alcohol if the purchaser is a minor or is under the influence of alcohol, drugs or any substance that might have similar effects. If the delivery is carried out by couriers, your agreement with the couriers should impose the obligation to verify whether the recipient of the goods is not a minor or intoxicated person.



*Note:* And the final advice from the lawyer was  that on 17th May 2022 it is expected that the Court will pass a judgment in one of the proceedings regarding  online alcohol sale, so she advised to wait for the decision in order to be sure about the whole model

_Citibank is bound by certain legal requirements to comply with sanctions and other legislation regarding payments to specific countries, individuals and entities.  Citibank acts as a participant of the payment process, and it has the right to request additional details._

_The purpose of a compliance check is to prevent terrorist financing and money laundering, and the legal basis for these is AML (anti-money laundering regulations). Section 11 of our standard T&Cs contain information on AML. These checks do not violate GDPR or any other regulations regarding personal data as we do not store the data, do not share it with any third parties and do not use it for any other purposes._

These compliance cases are common in all of the markets and usually these are resolved about in a week. Meaning in the future there might be more such compliance cases about our new drivers. This particular case is very rare that it has been taking so long time.

Adding Ellex LV response here as well. Our conclusion in another ticket was that Bolt’s age verification processes for alcohol sales are compliant with LV laws.

----

# _We understand that the point of sale in case of alcohol sales is considered the webpage / mobile phone application. Does this rule apply to Bolt Food as well? For background, our T&Cs outline that the sale agreement is only concluded between the restaurant / store and the customer. Bolt Food as an application only facilitates the sales and does not participate in the agreement between the customer and the restaurant / store._

Yes, in this case, the webpage / mobile phone application is considered the point of sale. You are also right that from a legal point of view the seller is restaurant and not Bolt Food. Accordingly, even if selling on Bolt Food platform, the restaurant is still obliged to verify customer’s age. Theoretically, if the restaurant cannot achieve it through own means, it should ask Bolt Food to implement measures that allow for age verification (the actual verification may be performed on restaurant’s behalf by Bolt or a third-party service provider), otherwise the restaurant is not allowed to perform distance sale of alcohol and risks an administrative fine up to 7100 € (and in case of repeated offences may lose the alcohol retail licence).

 

# We understand that in order to buy alcohol customers are required to identify themselves using AeS/QeS measures. On Bolt Food app the customer is obliged to confirm that he/she is at least 18 years old while purchasing alcohol, and upon delivery of the alcohol the ID of the customer is checked by the courier. Does Bolt Food currently comply with Latvian requirement to check the identity of our customer upon alcohol purchase?

 

Customer’s age must be verified twice – online before making the purchase and also in-person at the time of delivery. So the second step (delivery) seems to be okay but first step (online) is not compliant. Pursuant to Article 6.^1^(4) of the Law on Handling Alcoholic Beverages, the buyer’s identity must be verified using either:

# means of electronic identification that correspond at least to level “qualified” or “qualified increased security”;^1^ or

 

# strong customer authentication within the meaning of Article 4(30) of Payment Services Directive 2 (directive (EU) 2015/2366).^2^

^_____________________________^

^1^ The functional requirements for obtaining each of these levels are provided in [Cabinet of Ministers regulations No 560|https://likumi.lv/ta/en/en/id/293654-regulations-regarding-the-technical-and-organisational-requirements-for-the-qualified-and-qualified-increased-security-electronic-identification-service-provider-and-the-service-provided-thereby], but even the less stringent level “qualified” requires two different authentication factors, so the current system where the customer simply confirms (e.g., by use of check-box) that he/she is 18 years old does not comply with Latvian requirements.

^*2*^ Used by most online banking apps and there are third party service providers who provide this service to others for a fee (allegedly ~ 0,50 € per verification). Apart from Smart-ID we have also heard the names of “Contumatic”, “Veriff” and “Zippyid”.

Me and [~accountid:6052891960d39e006f72f0f0] have reviewed the proposed solution, and it is our opinion that the easiest way to solve this issue is to let restaurant own couriers to use our courier app. Otherwise we have no control over the couriers' ETA, no control over the fact whether the food was picked up by the courier, when the delivery will take place etc. Our customer support will be the one dealing with possible complaints being at the same time completely “blind” with regard to couriers' location or activities and all the anger with regard to possible faulty delivery in those cases will be managed by Bolt Food app. This does not sound like a good PR and we might end up with loads of unhappy customers.

For this case it is acceptable to not change T&Cs but conclude separate agreements with some restaurants just for the testing period (bears low legal risk).

If testing is successful, we would suggest the following steps:

* *Separate agreement template with partners*. Concluding separate agreements with partners who would like to use this feature. The contract should state among other things that 1) our current partner T&Cs apply to them and 2) our current courier T&Cs apply to them;
* *Updating user T&Cs*. We need to state that in some cases both restaurant and courier services are provided by the restaurants, and not by the independent couriers operating on our app. Please note that if we drop this feature after a couple of weeks, then we need to undergo the process of T&Cs changes once again (i.e., notify all the users and follow mandatory notice periods);

Hi Danielle, please find responses below 🙂

All my answers are given based on stock options, if any of these questions were asked by employees who have received CBU’s (cash based units, also known as phantom options) then answers might differ\!

*Question 1:* 
If I leave the company - how and when can I sell my stocks? - How will I be notified about an event and who will be my contact person at Bolt for this?

Once option holder leaves the company then if they are considered a good leaver they will keep all their vested units and unvested units will be returned to Bolt options pool. If leaver is considered a bad leaver then all units, both vested and unvested, will be returned to Bolt options pool. Both good and bad leaver considerations are explained in Confluence page. 
If option holder is about to leave the company or has already left then all the same rules and terms apply as for existing employees - exercising options is available 10 years after grant date or during a liquidity event. During liquidity events Company will contact all eligible option holders notifying them about the possibility to exercise their options early, for that email address entered to Carta are used so it’s really important that option holder would keep that up to date in the system. If 10 years has passed from the grant date then it’s the responsibility of the option holder to notify Company about their desire to exercise options by sending an exercise notice (attached to all grants in Carta) to the Company.

*Question 2:*
Do I have my options already? I haven't paid a strike price of 1 EUR for my shares as yet? Can this only be done after my options are fully vested?

Since i don’t know who asked that question then my answer is that most probably this person has been granted options 🙂 
Also important to note that options are not shares\!
Options are granted and these are vesting over period, first earn out happens 1 year after grant date (we have a 1 year cliff in place) and after that earn outs happen regularly, so if at least 1 year has passed from the employees option grant date then the employee has vested some of their options.
When paying strike price then options are converted to shares, this process is called exercising options. According to our option agreement exercising is allowed 10 years after grant date or during a liquidity event so currently it is not possible to exercise options (pay strike price and convert their options to shares).

*Question 3:* 
If I leave the company before my 4 year vesting period, what is the process in terms of buying the shares I have already vested?

Again, options are not shares\!
According to our option agreement exercising is allowed 10 years after grant date or during a liquidity event so currently it is not possible to exercise options (pay strike price and convert their options to shares). 
Once option holder leaves the company then if they are considered a good leaver they will keep all their vested units and unvested units will be returned to Bolt options pool. Good leaver will have the right to exercise their units according to our option agreement. If leaver is considered a bad leaver then all units, both vested and unvested, will be returned to Bolt options pool. Both good and bad leaver considerations are explained in Confluence page.

*Question 5:* 
Will moving abroad have any effect on my options/shares?

Bolt’s options are granted from group company located in Estonia, however, country specific taxes where the options holder lives apply as the tax an employee has to pay depends on their tax residency. Bolt cannot give any tax advise as the tax laws of countries may vary significantly and may depend on your personal circumstances, it is generally advisable to contact the tax advisers in countries concerned to make sure that taxes are properly paid.

*Question 6:* 
How does it work in terms of selling my shares? I have heard you can only sell 10% of your shares. How many times do we have the opportunity to sell? Once a year, month or week? If it's once a year, will it take 10 years before I can sell all of my shares for cash?

Bolt grants to its employees options, not shares. Options are not sellable, these need to be exercised (strike price needs to be payed) and during that options are converted to shares of the company, and shares are sellable. According to Bolt’s option agreement exercising is allowed 10 years after grant date or during a liquidity event, for example a secondary sale which is considered an early exercise (happening before 10 years has passed from the grant date). With early exercises the Company can set eligibility rules which need to be met in order to participate in the sale.
Regarding how often one can exercise their options and sell units then it’s hard to tell, during the past years we have had regular secondary sales taking place but it’s conditional to investors interest to buy shares so no guarantees of specific times can be made.

Details from [Anastasia’s deep dive|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1mgbMsoTkDxLMuUlW7HlePDnJY0VPy8qp9_FxjLhVIuk/edit#gid=276276169]:

*Main points:*

* Out of all ATI’s: ‘I’m having issues starting or finishing the ride’, ‘vehicle stuck in the snow’ was the most common issue at 52.6%. Out of those, the issue reoccurred in 64.6%.
* In 73.2% (93/127 cases) of stuck in snow cases, the vehicle wasn't hidden like it should've been.
* 67 vehicles were the cause of 507 users being stuck in the snow. Out of those, 47 vehicles required hiding but weren’t hidden, which caused 417 users to be unable to start their ride.
* Only 12.3% (20/163) of vehicles that weren’t hidden right away were successfully driven out of the snow by another user. - On average 2 (2.3) people encountered the problem before it was solved by another user.
* The average nr. of users who encountered an issue with the same vehicle is 8 (7.45), with the highest of 33 users on the same vehicle.
* Hyundai i20 was the most commonly stuck in the snow with 30% of total cars with the same issue.

*Propositions to decrease the ‘stuck in snow’ issue reoccurrence:*

* Create a new KB dropdown in a modified article 'issues starting a ride': ‘vehicle is stuck in the snow’ and introduce a guideline to hide the vehicle if the unsuccessful trip count (1.5€ charge in order history) is 3 or more. There is a 12% chance another user will be able to get the car out of the snow before that, so should the article be introduced and agents start hiding the vehicles earlier we can expect 87% of ‘vehicle stuck in snow’ reports. (166 users total contacted us, 145 could’ve been avoided had the car been hidden after the 2nd unsuccessful attempt).
* Check what could potentially be the reason for Hyundai i20s getting stuck more frequently than other vehicles. Low clearance perhaps? In general, the suck in snow issue could potentially be occurring with all vehicles due to BD cars using L/M tires suitable for all seasons instead of the winter-specific ones. Cars slide on slippery surfaces easier.

External counsel (OC IT) was instructed on 21 April. Here is there feedback:

*OC IT:* 

This is a binding proposal for a real estate lease agreement that Bolt submits to the real estate owner through the real estate agency. This type of contractual scheme is not atypical in the context of property leases, if real estate agencies are involved. Normally these types of offers are made on standard forms prepared by real estate agencies which, as in this case, do not excel in terms of completeness and clarity.

 Please find below our points:

* *Art. 3* – It is stated that the compliance of the installations of the real estate with the applicable regulations is "_to be verified_". Firstly, if current installations do not comply, scope of and timeframe for compliance works – which must be borne by the landlord – should be ascertained. Furthermore, if they are non-compliant, it is not clear how this aspect would be regulated in the final contract. Finally, you may also be inclined to choose a different property if there is too long timeframe for such compliance works.  
* *Art. 5* – It is unclear whether you have to provide a security deposit and/or a first-demand bank guarantee ("X"s are put in both boxes). The amount of this latter guarantee seems a bit excessive and not in line with market practice. Usually the amount of the security ranges from a sum equal to 1 month's rent to 6 months' rent. 
* *Art. 6* – As to the ancillary charges, it is stated that Bolt will pay them to the landlord as advance payments contextually to the payment of the rent – which is market practice – subject to adjustment at the end of the year. Two observations: (1) the exact amount of these advance payments is not indicated (and it should be); (2) it is not specified what kind of costs are involved.
* *Art. 8* – Please note that:
** It is stated that the agreement will have a 6+6 years duration (market standard). Nothing it is stated on withdrawal or termination. As to withdrawal ("_disdetta_"), we assume that the final agreement will provide for a 12-month notice period, as per Italian real estate lease rules. With reference to termination ("_recesso_"), the Italian real estate lease rules provides for a standard right to termination of the tenant, only in case of serious grounds. To this purpose, we suggest to negotiate Bolt's right of termination also in the absence of such serious grounds: this can be added to the offer under point 11, which refers to notes and additional clauses.
** Furthermore, the effective date of the final agreement is not precisely stated, nor is the date of delivery of the real estate property to Bolt. We think that effective date and delivery of the real estate shall occur on the signing date of the final agreement.
* *Art. 9* – Please refer to comment to art. 8 above on dates.
* *Art. 10* –  When submitting the offer – which is irrevocable for the next 20 days – Bolt must hand over the sum of EUR 3,300 to the real estate agent. This sum is then handed over to the landlord if he accepts your offer, thus becoming a "_caparra confirmatoria_". Having said that, it is not clear what happens to this amount if Bolt refuses to enter into the final lease agreement: since it is a _"caparra confirmatoria"_, under Italian law, we assume that this amount will be definitively kept by the landlord. In case Bolt enters into the final lease agreement, it is unclear whether this amount shall be considered as payment for the first month's rent or returned to Bolt. We assume that this will be regulated in the final agreement. In any case, you could propose to regulate this aspect explicitly in the offer, indicating that this amount will be considered as payment for the first month's rent.
* *Pages 4 and 5* – Please note that:
** The dates on pages 4 and 5 need to be updated.
** The part of Bolt's acceptance of the estate agency's mediation in these negotiations is also reported here. In addition to this acceptance, Bolt undertakes to pay the agent a commission of EUR 6,600 (plus VAT) upon conclusion of the "preliminary rental agreement". We assume that the term "_preliminary lease agreement_" refers this offer, if accepted by the landlord: this would mean that the agent would obtain its commission prior to the signing of the final agreement; on this point, you can try to negotiate that this commission is paid upon execution of the final agreement (it is one of the options provided in that list), although it may be difficult to amend this point... It remains understood that this amount will be returned to Bolt if this offer is not accepted.  

In addition to the above, we highlight that a series of lease-related aspects are not expressly regulated in this offer, such as: (i) rules on ordinary and extraordinary maintenance of the real estate property; (ii) rules on improvements, additions, fittings; (iii) the possibility of subletting and assignment of the final agreement; (iv) any condo charges, if the property is located within a condominium complex. We assume that these aspects will be expressly regulated in the final lease agreement, a copy of which you will receive when (and if) your offer is accepted by the landlord.

 ***

*Risto feedback:*

* limit the Art. 6 to ideally 2.5% but anywhere below 5% and should come from the CPI

* Art. 8, have an exit clause with a lowest notice period possible, ideally 3-months and without a serious cause. We can agree on “Bolt not being able to operate profitable in that city” but to use that clause only when it’s really needed.

* Art. 8/9 the delivery and start of the payment calculation should result from the signing of the acceptance act.

* Art. 10 we should be able to consider it as the first month’s rent

* Pages 4 and 5 we usually pay the amount once the contract has been signed
* rules on ordinary and extraordinary maintenance of the real estate property: we should add the clauses from our template which regulate the maintenance part for which the Landlord is responsible. Could you do that Emilie?

* the possibility of subletting and assignment of the final agreement: we’d like to have the acceptance from the Landlord to rent the premise out to 3PLs without the need from the Landlord to give acceptance (as we’ll be liable for the tenancy anyways).

*Emilie’s feedback on Risto' points:*

* +*maintenance of property:*+

 "the Landlord undertakes:

5.2.1 To ensure access to the Premises around the clock to any person indicated by Bolt;

5.2.2 +To maintain the Premises and the building the Premises are located at in a suitable condition for using the Premises for Intended Purpose and ensure the Premises and the building the Premises are located at has a usage permit and complies with all local laws+;

The Landlord acknowledges that uninterrupted electricity power is utmost necessity for Bolt for being able to use the Premises for its intended purpose any therefore any stoppages in providing the electricity is equated of not being able to use the Premises+;

5.2.5 +To eliminate all defects and damages for which the Landlord is responsible for under the Agreement, within 24 hours after becoming aware of such defect or damage. Should the Landlord neglect to do so, Bolt is entitled to eliminate the said defect or damage itself and claim the respective costs from the Landlord. According to the termination notice, you have decided to terminate the employment contract with Mr Skubis without observing the termination notice, i.e. with immediate effect due to the “unforeseen, long-term and repeated absences of the employee from work, requiring the employer to take organizational measures (appointing replacements) and entailing expenses for employing employees performing duties related to the managerial function of the employee.”

 

# *Long-term absence from work of Mr Skubis*

The termination notice mentions the following absence - from July 29, 2020 until the date of termination notice with a one-day break on June 1, 2021, when the employee reported leave on request.

 

The above calculation of the absence +*is wrong*+ and could not have constituted grounds for the termination of the employment contract without observing the notice period. Please note that the sick leave period prior to the “one-day break” on June 1, 2021 cannot be taken into account while calculating the absence period giving grounds for immediate termination of the employment contract.

 

# *Long term absence giving grounds to immediate termination of the employment contract*

Polish Labour Code allows the employer to terminate the employment contract with immediate effect in case the employee is absent due to his illness for period longer than 182 days. In case of Mr Skubis, the actual length of his absence due to latest illness (please note that we can calculate his latest illness from June 2, 2021 to November 30, 2021) is *181 days.* As a side note, the employee is questioning the fact that the employer had legal grounds to decline the leave on demand on December 1, 2022. Such decline might be acceptable only when the employer has strong proofs that the employee is abusing his right. In our case we cannot exclude the possibility that the employee “this time” tried to exercise his right in-line with the Polish Labour Code (even if on the following day he would have received another sick leave). During the court proceedings the employee may claim that the leave on demand was necessary due to e.g. family member illness or headache which would be enough to substantiate his request.

 

# *Necessity to sufficiently describe the reason for termination of the employment contract*

Irrespective of the above, Polish Labour Law imposes the obligation to sufficiently describe the reasons for termination of the employment contract. In our case, the termination notice contains reference to wrong article of the Labour Code and at the same time provides wide description mentioning both the long absence as well as the necessity to take additional organizational measures connected with such absence. In his claim, your ex-employee questions the reasons for the termination of his employment contract saying that those reasons are unclear, not precise and not true as none of those organizational troubles and necessity to incur additional costs did not take place during his sick leave. +Under Polish law the mere fact that it is not clear what was the actual reason for the termination of the employment contract is enough to lose the case.+

*To sum up:*

* Chances of Bolt winning this case are extremely low.
Due to procedural reasons, the termination may be recognized as  premature and the decline of leave on demand on December 1, 2021 as unjustified.
We can fully understand the frustration caused by long term absence intertwined by one-day holidays on demand. We confirm that above legal loop-hole is very often abused by employees and in such cases most often the courts rule in favour of the employees.
Taking into account the estimated timing (in Warsaw employment cases last even few years) costs involved in pursuing this case (not only the legal fees but also the time of Bolt’s staff, including Łukasz Stachowiak testifying as witness), we advise you to settle this case with Mr Skubis.

h3. _What if the user wants to delete the account due to an issue they experienced, e.g. an overcharge?_ 

_If the user specifies that they wish to delete their account due to an issue (and it is something we can solve), solve the user's issue first:_

* _Ask in your reply if they still wish to proceed with their account deletion and mention that if they don't get back to us, we will proceed with their account deletion. Put the ticket on-hold._
* _Leave an internal note in the ticket indicating that unless the user confirms otherwise, their account should be deleted once the ticket becomes open again (even if they did not get back to us)_
* _Once the ticket becomes open, continue with the next steps to delete the account._

I understand you wish to remove the {{cancelled}} enum value from both {{event}} and {{state}} columns, however, it is impossible to remove the value without causing table locks. The target tablespace sizes are as follows:

{noformat}1.7G taxify_rental_car_order_global/order_event.ibd
1.4G taxify_rental_car_order_global/order.ibd{noformat}

To remove the value without causing data corruption, the only option we have is using the MySQL native alter method which will rewrite the 1.7G & 1.4G to the tablespace. It might take several minutes to complete the alter and meanwhile, it will lock all transactions on the target tables. It will also cause several minutes of replication delay for all the replicas.

My suggestion is do not remove the value and just not use it.

In Live we provide 1 master and 2 slaves ( for read-only ).

In Live ProxySQL configuration setup, there are read query redirection rule sets:

{noformat}+---------+--------+--------------------+--------------+-----------------------+-------+
| rule_id | active | match_pattern      | re_modifiers | destination_hostgroup | apply |
+---------+--------+--------------------+--------------+-----------------------+-------+
| 1       | 1      | SELECT 1 AS PING   | CASELESS     | NULL                  | 1     |
| 2       | 1      | ^SET time_zone(.*) | CASELESS     | NULL                  | 1     |
| 100     | 1      | ROUTE READONLY=1   | CASELESS     | 1000000               | 1     |
+---------+--------+--------------------+--------------+-----------------------+-------+{noformat}

If a query matches with  {{match_pattern}} , in your case {{/* ROUTE READONLY=1 */}} , ProxySQL sends the query to either one of slave for READ.

The query below is an insert query, therefore it is perfectly normal to get an error message that it can not be executed.

The reason for Prelive works without an error is because there are no slaves in Prelive.

There is only one master therefore regardless of the Prelive ProxySQL query rules, it won’t be redirected.

Please remove {{/* ROUTE READONLY=1 */}} from DML queries.

According to the *Methodological norm for applying the provisions of the Law no. 319/2006 on safety and health at work*, _Article 19_: "in the case of enterprises and / or establishments with *more than 250 employees*, *the employer must organise one or more internal prevention and protection services*. If the internal prevention and protection services do not have the necessary capacities and skills to carry out all the prevention and protection activities provided in _Art. 15*_, *the employer must use one or more* *external services for those prevention and protection activities that the employer cannot carry out with his own staff*.”

Requirements for the *internal prevention and protection services*:

* (_Art 22_) The employer will determine the number of workers assigned according to the size of the enterprise and / or unit and / or the risks to which the workers are exposed, as well as their distribution within the enterprise and / or unit.
* The designated workers must have *mainly occupational safety and health responsibilities* and, at most, complementary duties.
* (_Art 20_) The nominal designation of the worker / workers to deal with prevention and protection activities is made by written decision of the employer.
* The employer will designate the worker only from among the workers with whom he has concluded an individual full-time employment contract.
* The employer shall record in the job description the prevention and protection activities that the designated worker has the capacity, the necessary time and the appropriate means to carry out.
* (_Art 21; Art. 49_) *In order to be able to carry out prevention and protection activities, the designated worker must meet at least the minimum training requirements in the field of occupational safety and health:* a) high school education (theoretical studies in real profile or technological studies); b) course in the field of occupational safety and health.
* (_Art. 24_) The internal prevention and protection service is organised under the *direct subordination of the employer as a separate structure*.
* Workers in the internal prevention and protection service should only carry out prevention and protection activities and at most complementary activities such as: fire prevention and extinguishing and environmental protection.
* The employer shall record in the internal regulations or in the organisation and functioning regulations the prevention and protection activities for the performance of which the internal prevention and protection service has adequate capacity and means.
* (_Art 26_) When the employer carries out his activity in several work points, the prevention and protection service must be organised in such a way as to ensure that the specific activities are carried out properly.



*Art 15 describes the prevention and protection activities to be carried out. It is a long list, let me know if you need it translated in EN.

+In agreement with the Constitutional Court:+
9.2 - As regards the provision of article 13, paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 of TVDERAA, it follows from the above that the diploma restricts the number of licenses that may be issued (or endorsed, in the case of entities already licensed at national level under Law no. No 45/2018, of 10 August) using the fixed structure of transport companies in the market: the licensing of the TVDE operator will not be legally admissible if the total number of vehicles of similar operators represents more than 5% of the total taxi fleet (of licensed companies) in each Azorean island (no. 1). Furthermore, by decision of the Regional Government, the authorised number of TVDE vehicles resulting from the application of the coefficient on the number of taxi vehicles may be modified for certain specific geographical areas, potentially restricting licensing to a greater extent in those territorial constituencies (paragraph 2).
Limiting the number of licences to be issued (or to be endorsed) means closing the market to new TVDE operators once the numerical value resulting from application of the coefficient fixed pursuant to paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 13 of the TVDERAA. Since access to the activity depends on licensing, the rule establishes, in effect, a numerus clausus of operators in the subsector. Thus, it prohibits the access of new agents to the passenger transport market under the TVDE regime, there is no doubt that this is a measure restricting the freedom of private initiative.
Finally, it should be recalled that Article 13(1) in fine of TVDERAA imposes another additional limit for companies to be in a position to access the market. As we said above, the investment in fixed capital cannot involve the incorporation in the company of more than three TVDE vehicles, under penalty of the agent being refused licensing, blocking access to the market. This is a limitation to business initiative on the financial aspect, since it results in the impossibility to implement a project guided by economy of scale. In fact, this legal measure constitutes a conditioning factor as to the investor's prospects of profitability and as to the time limit of recovery of the capital invested, thus operating a restriction on access to the sub-sector.
In line with what has been set out above on the perimeter of defence of the freedom of private initiative set out in Article 61(1) of the Constitution of the Portuguese Republic the normative programme contained in Article 13(1) and (2) of the TVDERAA constitutes a restriction to the scope of protection of the freedom of private initiative in the area analogous to rights, freedoms and guarantees (respecting the freedom to create a company and

Hello Erica,

Both of these rides belong to the same fraud pattern with JVSUA invite code. We’ve been looking into this last week and this week further, we know that +1600 rider accounts were involved and we have enough info to block +500 of them this week. 

* Both orders you sent were placed from the same area (maybe 20-30 meters apart).
* Both drivers were already at the pickup location before the orders were placed at 4 AM in the morning.
* The first driver 2590096 did not have any rides for more than 4 months and they came online to do this fraudulent ride.
* The second driver 1161660 came online just 1 minute before the order was placed.
* Both rides have signs of GPS issues/manipulation.

Another thing is, both of these rides had very little estimated price (10-13€) and the destination was not changed. Which means that the drivers did not follow the inapp route and drove to a different location than what the app showed. If riders request to driver to go to a different location, they need to make this change in the app too. Both driver and rider can change destination when needed. 

Last but not least, the second driver has two more fraudulent rides they did following the same pattern in that week: 
[https://westeurope-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/878891736/985038643|https://westeurope-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/878891736/985038643]
[https://westeurope-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/878846596/984973264|https://westeurope-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/878846596/984973264]

Based on these signs, we believe these are pre-arranged fraudulent trips and should not be refunded. However, we should refund the commissions here as we would not want to collect commission for refunded rides. For example: not sure about the commission percentage in Portugal but if it’s 20%,  then it would be 1214.3 * 20% = 242.86€ compensation for the first driver. Then same way the compensation can be calculated for 3 rides of the second driver. Local ops should be able to do these compensations.

Dear team,

Having discussed the issue of marketing Bolt Market on Bolt Food platform within the legal team, it is our opinion that large market share of Bolt Food in the Baltics is attracting extra scrutiny from competition watchdogs and thus we need to be more careful and prepared.

* However, our conclusion is that the market in the Baltics is not mature enough yet to attract hardcore competitive landscape assessments.
* To mitigate the competitive risks we need to start taking precautions about preferential treatment, and these precautions come in two shapes:
** (1) Transparency about preferential treatment on Bolt Food platform. Applicable laws require us to disclose:
*** how are we forming the ranking of providers on our platform,
*** that there are certain providers that are subject to preferential treatment (i.e. Bolt Market and key accounts, such as McDonald’s, KFC etc.),
*** what kind of data are we collecting from our providers, customers and couriers on the platform.

If we disclose the above, we have a chance to argue that yes, we are treating some providers better than others, but we are transparent about this, and all providers knew about that while entering into contracts with us.

* (2) Assessment if we could offer chance of similar treatment for others (for certain remuneration)The approach taken above is not legally bulletproof once we are approached by the competition authority or European Commission but it provides us with significantly more efficient defense than the approach to be taken without being transparent.



To-dos:

* Legal is planning to change T&Cs in the end of May. We will include provisions on transparency reflected above in our Partner T&Cs.
* Meanwhile, having marketing comms regarding Bolt Market on Bolt Food without being transparent poses quite some risk to our activities but we believe that since T&Cs are already undergoing amendments, we are able to run these marketing messages for a month without being fully transparent.

By default Bolt is the one making amendments to the menus, prices etc. on behalf of the Partner. In terms of liability, it does not matter whether the information is uploaded to the Partner Portal by Bolt or by the Partner. As this table is replicated from MySQL as immutable (so it is assumed record don’t change over time and don’t need to be updated; only new records are appended), it is stored in S3, as objects (Parequet files). It is already prepared for queries with Redshift, so you can simply use it. If you join it with a table from Redshift (non-ext schema), Redshift will load it into memory (the partitions as specified by filtering predicates) and do the JOIN within Redshift (no re-read table for each row). Using the hints from the linked documents you are safe and can query it and join with other tables. This table is particularly small and you can simply query it and do not care 🙂

In all cases and even if talking about only the liability from faulty b2b software I do agree that a liability gap should be introduced. E.g _“The liability of Bolt in connection with any loss or damage that Customer may incur as a result of using Bolt Business shall be equal to \[… euros].”_ Per contracting playbook approved by Nick Powell the number as such should be approved by the Regional Head of Sales.

But more importantly whatever deviation we’d agree in special terms it should be drafted narrowly, so that especially clause 6.3 was not affected - the liability limitation for drivers, couriers, etc, should remain in place.

Thank you\! The feature is not new, these automations have been in place for a while, allowing riders to be refunded as long as set automation conditions are met. What changed recently is that the automations affect driver earnings.

Dear Anton,



Thank you for the feedback. We from the Bolt tax team have seen this transaction as VAT taxable mainly because of the definitions of services in Estonian VAT Act (§2 (3) 3)) and the VAT directive (Article 25 (b)) which both state that 

_the obligation to refrain from an act, or to tolerate an act or situation_ can also be regarded as VAT taxable services. 



By receiving the termination fee the sellers take upon themselves an obligation to refrain from certain activities in certain jurisdictions. So it appears that the transaction would fall under these definitions and VAT should be added to the invoices. The other reason we have supported the view that it is safer to add VAT is the fact that in reality the fee also covers handing over of some goods which definitely is VAT taxable.



However, we have not looked at this issue in great detail so happy to discuss if you have substantiations to alternative views. I understand the point that we may want to regard this payment as some sort of compensation for losses but looking at the big picture the above definitions of the VAT legislation seem to cast some doubt to the waterproofness of this approach.



Kind regards



Tanel

Dear all,

 

I understand TXF would like to redirect payment from TXF Global to TXF Tech for tax reasons. In general it does not make a difference to Bolt which of the parties receives the physical payments under the TA, provided that all of the TXF parties agree to change the destination.

 

However, it might be that your request is misplaced for the following reasons and I would recommend you double-check with a tax lawyer:

 

The compensation under the TA is meant as a settlement for the loss of business which takes place to varying degrees for all of the TXF parties in MT, CY and TN. The compensation is stated as a single amount and not allocated to specific entities, as it is not relevant to Bolt how the TXF parties assess the shares of their respective businesses in the whole group. Under the TA, we agreed that the only entity with a +legal+ claim against Bolt is the MT Partner (TXF Tech), and that the payment will +technically+ be made to TXF Global for further distribution between the TXF parties as they see fit. These two agreements are for convenience and ease of processing, and do not affect the internal relationships between the TXF parties.

 

As between the TXF parties, we would expect that for tax and accounting purposes, each TXF party will account for and receive its own fair proportion of the compensation. It would then be up to each TXF party to decide how its share of compensation is reflected in its accounts, depending on local rules, and whether it will be received in cash, remain as a claim against whoever received the physical payment, or be settled in a different manner. In Estonia, although I am not a tax lawyer, I believe that the compensation would not be considered VAT-taxable revenue because it is not received for goods or services, but rather for the termination of a business relationship. This might be different in MT, TN and CY.

 

Best regards,

Anton

#!/bin/bash

CRIT=$1

SQL="SELECT /* DBA QUERY */ TABLE_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME, ROUND((AUTO_INCREMENT / (     CASE DATA_TYPE       WHEN 'tinyint' THEN 255       WHEN 'smallint' THEN 65535       WHEN 'mediumint' THEN 16777215       WHEN 'int' THEN 4294967295       WHEN 'bigint' THEN 18446744073709551615     END >> IF(LOCATE('unsigned', COLUMN_TYPE) > 0, 0, 1)   )) * 100, 0) AS AUTO_INCREMENT_RATIO FROM   INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS   INNER JOIN INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES USING (TABLE_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME) WHERE   TABLE_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'INFORMATION_SCHEMA', 'performance_schema')   AND EXTRA='auto_increment'   ORDER BY AUTO_INCREMENT_RATIO DESC LIMIT 1;"

RES=$(/usr/bin/mysql --defaults-file=/etc/mysql/debian.cnf mysql -Nce "$SQL")

DB=$(echo $RES | cut -d " " -f 1)
TBL=$(echo $RES | cut -d " " -f 2)
PCT=$(echo $RES | cut -d " " -f 3)

PERF_DATA="| autoincr_used_max=$PCT"

if [ $PCT -lt $CRIT ]
then
    echo "OK - MAX INCR $DB.$TBL $PCT% $PERF_DATA"
    exit 0
elif [ $PCT -gt $CRIT ] || [ $PCT -eq $CRIT ]
then
    echo "CRITICAL - MAX INCR $DB.$TBL $PCT% $PERF_DATA"
    exit 2
else
echo "UNKNOWN- "
exit 3
fi{noformat}

Hey [~accountid:5f1a8e14e5efc1001bf8ec6d], thanks a lot.

Actually legal team’s view is that one month is too long of a period to provide these refunds. There are two types of legal grounds that might oblige us to provide customers with refunds.

* *Statutory obligation*. We do not have a statutory obligation to provide customers with refunds, since the sale agreement is concluded between the partner and the customer. Thus, the partner is the one who has obligation to provide refunds under the law. We have mentioned in section 5.3 of our T&Cs that the client may also submit complaints to the partner or the courier directly. The obligation for the partner and the courier to provide refund to the customer arises from the law, and partner or courier shall be liable for refunding the customer if the meal is of low quality or deficient in any other ways.
* *Contractual obligation*. Bolt has taken on a contractual obligation to accept complaints of customers under section 5.1 of our T&Cs. However, Bolt has not expressly agreed to provide refund to any customers.

Following the above, Bolt has actually no obligation to issue any refunds to the customers. The refunds are currently being done as a gesture of good will to the customers to make their experience on the platform more pleasant, and not engage into any disputes with partners or couriers directly. Therefore, it is a business decision how many days shall we give to customers in order to provide their complaints.

We take care of transactional part and [payouts|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/invoicing-payment/payouts?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22external_client_id%22%3A472%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] to fleet are successful - we take care that everything that has been added to the balance will get paid out.

We use default value, but node-timeout lower, {{(5000 * 10) + 900}} which is around 51 sec.

So if master is not seen on replica > 1min, it won’t automatically failover. Which is expected I guess.

{noformat}# A replica of a failing master will avoid to start a failover if its data
# looks too old.
#
# There is no simple way for a replica to actually have an exact measure of
# its "data age", so the following two checks are performed:
#
# 1) If there are multiple replicas able to failover, they exchange messages
#    in order to try to give an advantage to the replica with the best
#    replication offset (more data from the master processed).
#    Replicas will try to get their rank by offset, and apply to the start
#    of the failover a delay proportional to their rank.
#
# 2) Every single replica computes the time of the last interaction with
#    its master. This can be the last ping or command received (if the master
#    is still in the "connected" state), or the time that elapsed since the
#    disconnection with the master (if the replication link is currently down).
#    If the last interaction is too old, the replica will not try to failover
#    at all.
#
# The point "2" can be tuned by user. Specifically a replica will not perform
# the failover if, since the last interaction with the master, the time
# elapsed is greater than:
#
#   (node-timeout * cluster-replica-validity-factor) + repl-ping-replica-period
#
# So for example if node-timeout is 30 seconds, and the cluster-replica-validity-factor
# is 10, and assuming a default repl-ping-replica-period of 10 seconds, the
# replica will not try to failover if it was not able to talk with the master
# for longer than 310 seconds.
#
# A large cluster-replica-validity-factor may allow replicas with too old data to failover
# a master, while a too small value may prevent the cluster from being able to
# elect a replica at all.
#
# For maximum availability, it is possible to set the cluster-replica-validity-factor
# to a value of 0, which means, that replicas will always try to failover the
# master regardless of the last time they interacted with the master.
# (However they'll always try to apply a delay proportional to their
# offset rank).
#
# Zero is the only value able to guarantee that when all the partitions heal
# the cluster will always be able to continue.
#
# cluster-replica-validity-factor 10{noformat}

If a scooter or e-bike is stolen and we are able to find, locate and recuperate the rental, the only need for a police report would be if the rental has been damaged in any way. If we file one and don’t report a loss of any kind, the police will all but guaranteed get back to us and ask what loss we have suffered and in that respect staff wages etc. is not considered a loss, it would need to be a loss directly related to the scooter itself.

If we cannot locate it or it is located somewhere we don’t have access to, then we need to report it. 

It is only Bolt that can report the rental stolen to the police. In terms of law, it is only the injured party who has the legal capacity to file such a report i.e. the one who has suffered a loss. The rental belongs to Bolt and thus Bolt is the only entity legally entitled to report it stolen. In laymen terms, no one can report somebody else’s property stolen, unless the injured party is a minor or legally incapacitated but that is obviously beyond the scope of this issue :).

[~accountid:5f1a8e14e5efc1001bf8ec6d] I can see all of the tickets came in from Zendesk hence I just used [Looker|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/explore/customer_support_product/ticket_comments?toggle=vis&qid=0uQbpTectbTyhqxdn13wvs] (as we surface comments there as well)

----

Deep-dive into CS tickets for the last week - 18 - 25 April & the issue type = I have an issue with my courier balance. 

In total CS solved ~900 tickets related to this & I’ve analysed roughly half of them. First let’s see where majority of the tickets are coming from:

!Screenshot 2022-04-29 at 15.44.37.png|width=755,height=547!

GH & AZ contribute ~70% of all tickets opened (620 out of 900) to CS. 

----

Then checking if the selected issue type is actually related to billing? We can see roughly half of the tickets aren’t related to courier balance at all - No includes questions from impatient couriers asking why doesn’t my balance update or why haven’t I yet received any payouts. But also complaints about invalid addresses & how can I activate new courier as a FO. So pretty much everything goes under _I have an issue with my courier balance_

!Screenshot 2022-04-29 at 15.51.08.png|width=479,height=299!

----

Analysing the issues in more detail obviously each ticket is different but we can bucket them by topic I’ve found the best:

!Screenshot 2022-04-29 at 15.58.47.png|width=482,height=296!

So the biggest one here is (as expected) complaints from impatient couriers asking: 

* why haven’t my balance updated? 
* where is my earnings? 
* why haven’t I received a payout? 
CS keeps copying the same answer asking to wait a couple of days as it doesn’t update instantly.

----

Next (& most interesting for us) is the questions about balance. I did a deep-deep dive into those requests:

!Screenshot 2022-04-29 at 16.02.27.png|width=479,height=296!

The vast majority of questions are related to negative balance - this includes questions: 

* why do I have negative balance? 
* how to pay Bolt to decrease my debt? 
* I’ve worked very hard last week but my balance is still negative, why? 
* how can I check my negative balance? 
* how to keep my balance positive?
* I don’t recognise an entry on my balance (e.g. bag deposit)

But also why I’m not receiving any cash orders & my balance is incorrect (which needed some adjustments). In general this type of tickets are solved pretty quickly (only a couple of replies from CS) discussing 1) cash orders 2) fees from Bolt (e.g. delivery bag). But I think there’s definitely room for improvement how the courier balance shows on courier app 

----

Third most popular topic was issues related to refund hence I did a deep dive into that as well:

!Screenshot 2022-04-29 at 16.12.16.png|width=478,height=295!

Pretty much all of those tickets were about deliveries which weren’t completed & due to that the courier balance had a negative entry. CS keeps coping the same answer to the couriers which goes something like: please dispose the order into a bin & send us pictures of it - after this we can remove the negative balance entry. I think here’s another point for improvement - if the courier cannot complete the delivery there should be a button for this in the app which automatically gives instructions & opens a camera on their phone. This way we wouldn’t receive so many of these questions. 

----

Coming back to GH & AZ here’s the issue type breakdown for both of them: 

!Screenshot 2022-04-29 at 16.19.06.png|width=479,height=298!

!Screenshot 2022-04-29 at 16.19.20.png|width=481,height=297!

----

So in conclusion we can say the things aren’t actually that bad for billing as there’s a lot of tickets closed with invalid issue type (not related to billing at all) & we would have to improve our communication to explain after making a payment the balance isn’t updated immediately (or improve the speed how quickly the payment reaches to our system such that balances update quicker). On a billing point-of-view we could analyse how the balance section shows on courier app & make it clearer for everyone (same for the orders not delivered)

I’m always a bit reluctant to add content which is designed for non-legal purposes [such as this explanation|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BFB/pages/2235859265/Credit+Payment+Terms]. Especially if it doesn’t provide any additional value compared to what is already provided for in the [default special terms|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1wT9xRPC07hAYnFUd7RJV-dwXf2wb5qk5vdEParroo9U/edit] - credit limit is already included, also the fact that it’s monthly, and also what happens if the the Customer doesn’t pay up, etc. I trust what happens if the credit limit is reached is implied but surely we can elaborate that if this is the case then further requests for Bolt Services would be rejected.

*But ofc if no legal risk then we can add whatever to the special terms.* 

However in this case the first question which crosses me is “Company - our client will always pay *the amount which equals the sum of all rides* of its *employees*.” Should be changed to “Users” as employees is a narrower term and might give ground to unwanted arguments by the Customer. Also it does not touch the fact that Customer has to pay Service Fee, and use other services than Rides - if applicable. 
So all in all I think this is where a bdm needs to be reasonable and explain this to the Customer and we accept only the must have clarifications. It’s always easier for a bdm to ask whatever internally. 🙂 

Cheers,

Note for planning tomorrow: I would like this task to lead in a direction where we have a good plan for how to do the validations for any features that we might have in the future rather than a simple fix that will just work. We touchbased this with Bruno a while ago, and the current status is we have 3 layers of validations:

# Front end
# Backend auto-validation
# Backend custom validation



If we need to validate a field by running an sql query or making a service call, it is problematic because the front end doesn’t check for it by default, and if there is automatic validators enabled the check won’t run in the backend either if the request is invalid. (e.g. a user might see invalid name with max length error, then once this is fixed the error might turn into phone number is invalid after caused after some db check)



Since this task is here and nobody objects to its existence, it is clear that we agree on doing the validation at once, however it would be good to document the way we prefer to do the validation once decided, so we do not have to rethink for the same problem in the future.

I catch up with [~accountid:61cc1c959ee70a00680edd89] today and understand that this deal will probably go ahead despite the legal risks. 

Considering that one of the high risks of this contract is the 15% penalty, we thought it would be useful to seek local advice (none of us being German lawyers). Andersen (German law firm) just reverted with their advice (+limited to the 15% penalty clause+) - please see their comments below:

* +_Clause V 2 used by Audi in its purchase agreement is generally permissible. The use of such a clause is quite common_+_._

_Brief background: In a decision in 2010, the Federal Court of Justice (Bundesgerichtshof - BGH) declared an identical clause also in a vehicle sale to be valid (BGH NJW 2010, 2122). However, in the case to be decided by the BGH, the difference was that the lump-sum damages were only_ *_10% and not 15%._* _This was deemed to be appropriate._

_The decisive factor was that the contractual partner (here: you) is permitted to prove that no damage was incurred at all or that the damage was significantly lower than the lump sum. This is the case here._

_In a case regarding antitrust violations the BGH allowed lump-sum damages in general terms and conditions of up to 15%. Whether or not the 15% level should only apply in antitrust law or also in general is unresolved. In the event that a claim for damages is actually asserted, the 15% lumpsum can be disputed._

* _Regarding your query_ +_whether or not this applies to all cases in which you can not accept the cars_+_:_

_In principle, yes, but the different scenarios must be carefully distinguished here. A distinction must be made between the assertion of damages (Geltendmachung von Schadensersatz) and the assertion of the claim for performance (Geltendmachung des Erfüllunganspruchs)._

_What does this exactly mean:_

_If you are unable to pay for the vehicles because you have_ *_not_* *_yet_* _received the money from the bank, the seller can initially only assert its so-called claims for performance. This means that it can only demand payment of the purchase price. Since this does not constitute a claim for damages, the 15% penalty cannot be charged._

_If, on the other hand, you are unable to pay for the vehicles_ *_at all_* _(because you will not receive any money from the bank at all) and you are therefore forced to withdraw from the purchase agreement, the seller can assert claims for damages. This may then be subject to a lump sum of 15%. If you can prove that the damage is less, a lower amount will be due._

_In other words, the clause is intended to protect the seller from producing the vehicles and you canceling the purchase agreement after the production._



I trust this is helpful but please let us know should you wish to discuss further or if you’d like us to instruct Andersen for a full review of this German contract.

Maksu- ja Tolliamet on edastanud Bolt Technology OÜ-le maksumenetluses tähendust omavate asjaolude kindlakstegemiseks teabe andmise korralduse, et kontrollida maksukohustuslase poolt saadud teabe vastavust tegelikkusele. 

Vastavalt makuskorralduse seaduse § 61 lõikele 3 märgitakse kolmandalt isikult teabe nõudmiseks korraldusse maksukohustuslase nimi või muud identifitseerimist võimaldavad andmed, kelle maksuasjaga seoses teavet kogutakse. Antud asjas on korralduses kinnitatud, et maskukohustuslaseks on TT Invest OÜ (registrikood 12014786). 

Küsitud andmed puudutavad aga füüsilist isikut ehk Bolt Food rakenduse kasutajat. Seega ei väljastaks Bolt andmeid maksumenetluse osalise ehk maksukohustuslase TT Invest OÜ kohta, vaid Bolt Food rakenduse kasutaja kui füüsilise isiku kohta. Samuti võib nimetatud aadressidele (J. Vilmsi tn 6-6, Tallinn ning Haraka tn 6-2, Tartu) tellimusi olla teinud mitu Bolt Food rakenduse kasutajat. Vastavalt isikuandmete kaitse üldmäärusele (EL 2016/679) peab isikuandmete töötlemine olema eesmärgipärane, minimaalne ja töötlemiseks peab esinema üks artikkel 6 lõikes 1 toodud õiguslikust alusest. Isikuandmete vastutava töötlejana peame olema veendunud, et füüsiliste isikute kohta isikuandmete väljastamiseks eksisteerib konkreetne seadusest tulenev õiguslik alus. Kuna küsitud andmeid ei puuduta maksukohustuslast TT Invest OÜ vaid füüsilisi isikuid, kes antud aadressidele tellimusi on teinud, siis ei ole Bolt vastutava töötlejana veendunud, et küsitud ulatuses isikuandmete väljastamine on eesmärgipärane ning väljastamiseks eksisteerib konkreetne seadusest tulenev õiguslik alus.
