Hi,

The payment has been now reversed.

Looking at the ratio of invoices generated vs tickets opened the Business vertical pops up by having much higher ratio - in March roughly 3 tickets were opened per 100 invoices (~3%) whereas for delivery this comparison was 0.1 tickets per 100 invoices. But as the vertical is relatively small the issues can easily be overlooked (e.g. for March only ~400 tickets were opened by business account Admin vs thousands from RH).

Obviously the Business vertical is slightly different vs others hence the number of tickets/invoices issued is much higher. Firstly we generate only one business invoice per month hence the absolute number of invoices for business is much smaller (as the rides invoices taken with business account go under Rides invoices). Hence even 1 ticket has much bigger affect on the ratio compared with e.g. Delivery (where we roughly generate 2 invoices per order). The other reason for such high rates could be that business admin actually opens up & checks the invoice more thoroughly as they are running a business & every payment has to be confirmed (+ other legal obligations) & if there’s any questions this will be flagged to our CS. Comparing this with e.g. Rides where regular user never even opens up the invoice hence they wouldn’t know if the info on the invoice is correct or not. And finally the communication between the business admins & our CS is easier. I think reaching out to Bolt as a business client is much easier than as a driver/courier etc.

Now, I’ve taken a deep-dive into the tickets opened up in March 2022. In total ~400 tickets were analysed the results are below: 

----

Checking the incoming tickets per country we see relatively equal share of all countries with Estonia, Kenya & Lithuania contributing ~50% of all tickets. This could be because in Estonia & Lithuania we have more businesses vs other countries hence more clients who could raise a ticket.

!Screenshot 2022-05-03 at 10.49.03.png|width=479,height=298!

----

Checking the Beehive issue types there isn’t a good breakdown for Business - there’s only 3 separate topics agent can choose. _I have an issue with my invoice_ has the majority which is also the widest topic - as seen below all different issue types go under that selection.

!Screenshot 2022-05-03 at 10.52.06.png|width=799,height=494!

----

Taking a deeper look into the tickets & actually checking what’s the reason behind the request we can see ~1/3rd of tickets were opened because client has completed a payment but it isn’t showing on the business company’s balance - taking a quick tour in {{#commerce-support-partner-payments}} channel we can see similar trend where roughly 1/3rd of messages are related to payment matching for business clients (we can say the same for our {{#commerce-support-billing }}Slack channel / Business queue in Jira):

!Screenshot 2022-05-03 at 10.55.07.png|width=793,height=491!

The other popular topics are:

* Not receiving monthly invoice (10.7% from all) - this is a communication issue as clients are unaware they can download the invoice & rides.csv from the BP & we only generate monthly invoices (once per month). 
* Unknown charge - service fee (9.4% from all) - another communication issue as clients are unaware the service fee clause is included in the terms & conditions. As far as I understood from the comments several clients had NO IDEA that Bolt charges service fee per each ride & several of them wanted account deletion after learning this. Same goes with CC accounts as there was an unknown charge from the credit card (& clients complained as they haven’t taken any rides during that day).
* Updating accounts details (7.3% from all) - I think this is a BP/Admin limitation as there was a lot of requests to update account’s details e.g. company name, VAT code etc. These are forwarded to local OPS to update the info in Admin & BP.

----

Checking the real issue types per country we can see majority is taken up by payment matching:

!Screenshot 2022-05-03 at 11.09.08.png|width=617,height=382!

!Screenshot 2022-05-03 at 11.09.15.png|width=478,height=296!

!Screenshot 2022-05-03 at 11.09.23.png|width=477,height=295!

In Estonia 🇪🇪  I think the holidays in Feb need to be taken into account as the due date & the Independence day overlapped hence the transactions took longer between the banks. Also clients (heavily) complained about the service fee by calling the police & deleting their accounts. 
In Kenya 🇰🇪 the users follow the same trend as in Rides & Delivery by quickly reaching out after the payment is done. The tickets were solved relatively quickly (1-2 comments) by saying we’ve reached out to the specific team (partner-payments) to match the payment with the account. I think it’s also a cultural thing as majority of the conversations were polite & they just wanted to let us know the payment has been done. 
In Lithuania 🇱🇹 we have a mixture of issues but in addition to the topics discussed above we see the business clients are not understanding the invoice - they don’t understand how much they have to pay (this includes CC companies) - maybe there’s something lost in translation? But also several clients asked why the ride doesn’t surface in BP - it was taken using the personal payment method hence it won’t be included to the business invoice.

*Main info:*

Unlike with Rides, we can’t offer a certain sum off of the order. We can offer:

* % menu discount. Specific caps are not currently supported (min, max)
* A base delivery discount (100% discount — note, that absolute value can differ per provider if they have a custom setup for fees)
* A full delivery discount

Promo codes can be further limited to:

* Time of day
* First X orders
* Specific providers
* Order recency per provider/vendor

*How does it work?*

Eaters have to enter the promo code in the Promo codes section in the profile & then the system checks certain criteria to check the validity and the parameters. of the promo code. 


NB\! Even if the code seems valid when the eater enters it, when they go to the home page they still might not be able to use it if the promo code is valid just for users who haven’t ordered from a certain provider in X amount of time. 

*How is it displayed?*

For regular restaurants, it will look like a regular promo with an “-XX%” or a “€0.00 delivery” badge on the home page, and discounted prices in the restaurant view. However, at this time discounts can’t be properly shown in the grid layout (= Bolt Market layout), so the eater will simply see prices that have already been discounted once they open the item and at the checkout. 

When a promo code is entered in the box, it displays a message that the code can be used for e.g. First ever Bolt Food order to get free delivery. 

*Error messages*

Error messages are displayed if the code is entered incorrectly, the code has expired, the account is not eligible…

Upon the subsequent resale by Bolt Operations OÜ to Bolt LE stores, inter-company invoices and payments should be prepared. The resale of the service to Bolt Store EE should be with 20% VAT, whilst the sale to non-EE stores will be with 0% VAT for Bolt Operations OÜ and reverse charge with the local territory VAT.

Can I set out the additional information here? So regarding any additional legal requirements for promotion via social media/online ads/physical advertising etc:

PL:

+*I. Alcohol*+

The general rule that promotion of alcohol (besides beer) is forbidden is binding regardless of the medium used.

However, there are some specific rules on promoting beer; it cannot be promoted:

* on the television, radio, cinema, or theater between 6 a.m. – 8 p.m., excluding advertisement made by competitive or professional sports event organizer, during this event
* on videotape or any data carrier (USB stick, CDs etc.)
* on newspaper/magazine/journal’s cover
* on advertising pole, billboard’s and other fixed or movable surfaces used for advertising, unless 20% of the advertising area is occupied by visible and legible inscriptions informing about the harmfulness of alcohol consumption or about the ban on selling alcohol to minors

There are no literal restrictions re. online promotion. However:

* As the restrictions are not very precise and are quite broad, internet website or social media wall could be considered the same as the newspaper/magazine/journal’s cover. 
* As we mentioned in questionnaire, the advertisement cannot be directed to minors; Thus, the most common practice is that in case of online promotion the user must 1) declare being at least 18 years before the website with ads is displayed to him or 2 ) register on the website and declare during registration that the user is at least 18 years old

+*II. Non-prescription medicine*+

There are no regulations strictly on online-promotion. The non-prescription medicine promotion can be audiovisual, audio or visual. Depending on on type, it must meet slightly different requirements.

*In case of audiovisual ad*:

* It must contain a warning in polish: “_Przed użyciem zapoznaj się z treścią ulotki dołączonej do opakowania bądź skonsultuj się z lekarzem lub farmaceutą, gdyż każdy lek niewłaściwie stosowany zagraża Twojemu życiu lub zdrowiu.”_ (Meaning: _“Before use, read the package insert or consult your doctor or pharmacist as each drug used improperly threatens your life or health.”_)

* The warning needs to be placed on the bottom of ad, and it has to cover at least 20% of the ad’s surface;
* The text must stand out from the background, be visible, legible, stationary, placed horizontally, and the distance of the letters from the bottom and top edges of the advertising background may not be greater than 1/2 of the height of the letters, and the distance between the lines of the inscription may not be greater than the height of the letters;
* must be read clearly in Polish and displayed on the screen for no less than 8 seconds.

*In case of audio ad:*

* It must contain a warning in polish: "_Przed użyciem zapoznaj się z treścią ulotki dołączonej do opakowania bądź skonsultuj się z lekarzem lub farmaceutą, gdyż każdy lek niewłaściwie stosowany zagraża Twojemu życiu lub zdrowiu._" (+the same warning as in case of audiovisual ad+)

* The warning needs to be read clearly in Polish, and the time of reading it cannot be shorter than 8 seconds;

*In case of visual ad:*

* It must contain a different warning than in case of audio/audiovisual ads: _"Przed użyciem zapoznaj się z ulotką, która zawiera wskazania, przeciwwskazania, dane dotyczące działań niepożądanych i dawkowanie oraz informacje dotyczące stosowania produktu leczniczego, bądź skonsultuj się z lekarzem lub farmaceutą, gdyż każdy lek niewłaściwie stosowany zagraża Twojemu życiu lub zdrowiu."_ (ENG: _"Before use, read the leaflet, which contains indications, contraindications, adverse reactions and dosage data, and information on the use of the medicinal product, or consult your doctor or pharmacist, as any medicine used inappropriately poses a risk to your life or health."_)
* The warning should be placed:
** at the bottom of the advertisement, on a plane constituting not less than 10% of its surface;
in such a way that the text stands out from the background plane, is visible, legible, stationary, placed horizontally, with the distance of letters from the lower and upper edge of the background plane of the advertisement not exceeding 1/2 of the height of the letters, and the distance between the lines of the inscription not exceeding the height of the letters.
In the case of an advertisement directed to the public in visual form covering more than one page, the warning shall be placed on the first page.

+Besides aforementioned additional requirements, our advice stays the same.+

+*Please note*+ this week it was announced it is planned that from 1^st^ January 2023 there will be new regulations on medicine advertisement. The previous advice considers +*current regulations.*+

RO:

The only medium specific ban is the one on advertising spirit drinks on outdoor media (i.e. bilboards and other street signage), or any type of alcoholic drink within 200m from schools and hospitals, in publications or shows addressed to minors (these would include online/social media, children addressed webpages and apps, as well), on the covers of press materials and public transport tickets.

In general, to be on the safe side, any online ad related to alcohol should entail obtaining a confirmation that the person visiting the website/social media account/installing a certain app which does not have a separate alcohol section is over 18 years old.

The rest of the restrictions would apply in the same way regardless of the medium used.

In general, the agreement is governed by EE laws, not RO.

One aspect which needs to be considered is Art. 1 para. 4 of the EU Interest & Royalties Directive: A company of a Member State shall be treated as the beneficial owner of interest or royalties only if it receives those payments for its own benefit and not as an intermediary, such as an agent, trustee or authorised signatory, for some other person.  Therefore, Bolt Holdings should make sure that the loan facility is/was actually offered by Bolt Holdings (i.e. the funds are made available by Bolt Holdings), for the entire duration for which the interest exemption is claimed (i.e. the assignment should be an instrument certifying the change of the economic substance of the loan as of 1 January).

From a procedural perspective, please note that the exemption claim is subject to an affidavit which needs to be signed by Bolt Holdings and kept by both parties to the loan, via which Bolt Holdings declares that it meets the conditions provided by the EU Interest & Royalties Directive (please find attached the bilingual form which also details all the conditions to be met). The affidavit needs to be accompanied by Bolt Holding's fiscal residency certificate, and needs to be restated along with the (annual) renewal of the fiscal residency certificate.

This is in RO but trust your external RO tax advisors can assist with completing it.

Hey [~accountid:619df38fc75da8007295630e] \! 

Some initial feedback and additional questions from privacy side to move on with the project. 

# *Legal basis*

The most suitable *legal basis* for processing these recordings would be legitimate interest - this means that *it would not be based on respective user’s consent.* Consent would not be suitable as the main reason for the processing is connected to ensuring safety of both riders and drivers, and in a conflict or possible conflicting situation asking for the other party’s consent for recording the situation will most likely not work. Only problem with this → Nigeria as one of the test markets does not have legitimate interest as a legal ground, so the only alternative is consent. How to incorporate this needs further assessment based on the Nigerian Data Protection Regulation. 

*2. Transparency and notification.* At minimum we should update our drivers and passengers privacy notices around this feature. Additional mean for delivering on the notification side → add information (e.g. with microphone icon) that the driver/rider may record the audio of this ride for safety reasons. 

*Questions:*

# *Where are we going to store these recordings?* In the file I see that there is an idea of storing them locally in user’s device? Or do we store it in our servers right away?
# *How long will we store it*? I.e. is the 24h time period to raise a safety case something that we will stick to? From privacy perspective - the shorter the time period of storing, the better. E.g. we have to be ready, that we must fulfil the data subject’s request for copy of this recording. Before doing so we must go through the recordings and if necessary, redact parts of it (e.g. there are two riders in the vehicle who discuss something private and the driver later requests a copy of the recording). We cannot deny the access to the copy altogether, but we can redact parts of it. This requires manual work (and may still be subject to errors), so better to store these for a minimal period of time. 
# *How long would we want to store the recording in case a safety report is initiated?* 
# *Will the recording start only when the rider/driver initiates the recording* (“pushes the button in the app”) and when will it end? Or are we still thinking about the idea of recording every trip if the user has enabled this feature? The last one is very privacy intrusive and hard to argue that we have legitimate interest to record every trip. Therefore my suggestion is to give the user the decision power on starting the recording case by case. This would support our argument that recording the trip was also in the legitimate interest of the driver/rider who felt unsafe.

I have been reviewing the attached document and here are my conclusions:

 

+*Regarding the Proposal as Official Mobility Partner*+  

Nothing to say, it’s just a summary of the package benefits for the Sponsor. No obligations or liability arise from this document. 

 

+*Regarding the participation contract,*+ it only contains the terms and method of payment, and it refers to the T&Cs: [https://www.des-show.com/app/uploads/tc-des-2022.pdf|https://www.des-show.com/app/uploads/tc-des-2022.pdf]

After reviewing the T&Cs, I do not see any red flags from a legal perspective. However, there are numerous provisions related to the dynamics and rules of the exhibition that must be read carefully by the business. I strongly recommend you to have a look at the link copied above.

Please see below a brief summary of what I consider relevant from a strictly legal point of view, but note that no responsibility is derived from these T&C, except as regards the registered trademark (explained in more detailed below): 

 

*_Payment_* 

* _1st Payment Term: 50% of the total Participation Option cost, contracted at the signature must be paid with a due date of 10 days from the issued Organizer’s invoice._  
* _2nd Payment Term: remaining 50% of the total Participation Option cost, contracted plus additional space or booth sqm (if it is the case), must be paid on 15th March 2022 with a due date of 10 days._ 

_In case of non-compliance of the payment conditions, the Organizer shall be entitled to offer the space booked for any other applicant company._ 

_The Organizer is entitled to reject Exhibitors, in its own discretion, in case the Participation Contract is not followed by the payment of the first invoice. Failure to sign the Participation Contract, or the failure to pay the first invoice, grants The Organizer the right to reject the request._ 

 

*_Withdrawal_* 

_Bolt has the right to withdraw from the event by communicating it to the Organizer with a registered letter with proof of receipt (forwarded in advance by email) within the following conditions:_  

_Before 11th February 2022: the Organizer will have the right to withhold 50% of the total cost of the Participation Option contracted. The Organizer as an indemnity will allocate half the amount to offset the costs incurred by the withdrawal and as a sign of goodwill, the other half would be regarded as a deposit by the Exhibitor in the case of desire to participate in the next edition of The Event._  

_After 11th February 2022: Bolt will be required to pay 100% of the total cost of the Participation Option and all set and installation costs for the services ordered and/or performed on the booked site, all taxes paid on behalf of Bolt as well as any damages the Organizer and/or the Event may suffer due to said withdrawal. The Organizer as an indemnity will allocate half the amount to offset the costs incurred by the withdrawal and as a sign of goodwill, the other half would be regarded as a deposit by the Exhibitor in the case of desire to participate in the next edition of the Event. In both withdrawals instances the Organizer in any case reserves the right to allocate the stand to another Exhibitor, without this possible allocation in any way prejudicing or limiting its right to request the indemnities described above._ 

*_VAT considerations_* 

F_oreign Exhibitors liable for taxation are not required any longer to pay the VAT on participation fee, stand fee and services connected with the event, with the exclusion of non-commercial Companies; in order to identify the type of Exhibitor (Company liable for taxations/non-commercial Company or private individual), before the issuing of the invoice it is essential to receive the VAT number/ID code proving the status of company and not of private individual._  

_Entrance tickets will still remain subject to Spanish VAT for all exhibitors (Spanish and international)._ 

 

*_Forbidden Activities_*  

_Any activity that may be detrimental to, disturb or harm the normal running of the Event is forbidden._  

_The following activities are absolutely prohibited: a) distribution of flyers in the pavilion corridors or outside the stand area; b) any kind of expression that due to its outward appearance or form may represent direct comparison with another Exhibitor; c) the distribution and delivery of any technical-informative and advertising material (magazines, manuals, books, brochures or anything else) not strictly pertinent to the Exhibitor, who may however distribute or deliver advertising material as long as it is strictly pertinent to his business sector, solely on his own stand; d) posters referring to calls for tender by bodies, organisations, newspapers, weekly or specialist magazines may not be displayed even on stands without prior written authorisation from The Organizer; e) broadcast of advertising messages; f) any type of flashing or variable lighting; g) permanence on the stands or in the area of the Event during closing hours without permission; h) any kind of sales to the public with immediate delivery; i) drawing, copying and photographing objects without written authorisation from the Exhibitor. The Organizer however reserves the right to directly reproduce or to authorise reproduction of group views or close-ups, external or internal and also to permit sales by officially authorised personnel. The Organizer cannot however be held responsible for any unauthorised photographs or filming by third parties._ 

 

*_Company Trademark Registration_*  

_Bolt is required to have regularly registered, patented or licensed the trademarks of the products that it intends to put on show in the exhibition space. If the trademark is pending patent, Bolt must issue to The Organizer a special statement in which it assumes all responsibility for any consequences ensuing from the use of the trademark itself, freeing and clearing The Organizer and any connected companies against any claims from third parties._  

_Bolt undertakes as follows:_  

# _not to show any product involved in an intellectual property dispute whereby the final judgement ruled against the Exhibitor; and_  
# _not to display prototypes and/or objects with trademarks, logos, decorations unless the Exhibitor has obtained all Intellectual Property Rights._  

_By signing the Participation Contract, Bolt assumes all criminal and civil responsibility for everything exhibited on its stand and releases The Organizer from all liabilities in the event that other economic parties claim industrial and/or intellectual property of the products in question. Bolt also assumes responsibility for checking if its own rights are breached by other Exhibitors at the Event and agrees not to advance any claims to The Organizer for any damage caused by breach of this provision._ 

 

*_Insurances_* 

_A Civil Liability and Property Damage Insurance Policies are included in all the Participation Options inclusive of the following:_  

* _Civil liability_ 
* _Damage to materials, excluding theft/robbery_

Hi [~accountid:6215e9dd505e68006ad66718] 

In relation to your question, currently, the legal provision in force is provided in Law no. 321/2009 on the sale of food products, which indeed requires a *maximum 14 working days payment term for fresh food, applied as of the moment when the merchandise is received*. Fresh foods is defined as follows: meat (except frozen products), fish and seafood (except frozen products), bakery and confectionary products (except for packaged and/or frozen products), eggs, milk, fresh perisahable vegetables and fruit (except frozen products).

The Romanian Parliament recently passed Law no. 81/2022 implementing Directive 2019/633 on unfair trading practices in business-to-business relationships in the agricultural and food supply chain.

This Directive applies to certain unfair trading practices (derived from imbalanced bargaining power) which occur in relation to sales of agricultural and food products by:

(a) suppliers which have an annual turnover not exceeding EUR 2 000 000 to buyers which have an annual turnover of more than EUR 2 000 000;

(b) suppliers which have an annual turnover of more than EUR 2 000 000 and not exceeding EUR 10 000 000 to buyers which have an annual turnover of more than EUR 10 000 000;

(c) suppliers which have an annual turnover of more than EUR 10 000 000 and not exceeding EUR 50 000 000 to buyers which have an annual turnover of more than EUR 50 000 000;

(d) suppliers which have an annual turnover of more than EUR 50 000 000 and not exceeding EUR 150 000 000 to buyers which have an annual turnover of more than EUR 150 000 000;

(e) suppliers which have an annual turnover of more than EUR 150 000 000 and not exceeding EUR 350 000 000 to buyers which have an annual turnover of more than EUR 350 000 000.

Based on this enactment, big retailers in Romania have already started sending inquiries to their food suppliers in relation to their turnover. The new law will be applicable to new agreements, while existing ones will need to be adjusted starting with 1 January 2023.

Our external counsel are in contact with the Competition Council, as many provisions are not clear (e.g. the 14 working days deadline mentioned by Law no. 321/2009, is under Law 81/2022 14 days over the contractual term). There is also the fact that the above turnovers are to be calculated at group level, but there is no indication on what approach will be preferred if various verticals within one company do not act as a single economic unit, in the sense of competition law (e.g. Bolt market and ridehailing).

Hi, Team. Is there any feedback?

*Project dependencies:*

* Main dependency: Quality team creation - they would drive outlier improvements (CSAT, MKA, issue tagging, QA scores).
* Suppliers have different ways of managing agent performance and so does in-house although most likely the way in-house manages outliers is not so structured as suppliers'. 
* There’s an opportunity to align agent performance mgmt system across all companies, however, it shouldn’t be on the L&D to do that.
* A new set of KPIs and targets are currently being developed.

*Final conclusions:*

* It makes sense for us to focus on developing a dashboard for L&D mostly.
* With all the changes that may happen soon, it doesn’t make sense for us to create a dashboard for TLs and agent performance mgmt system.
** However, when the QA function is going to be created, we can provide our input on how the system can look like so that it’s aligned with onboarding.
* Competency-based models - again, it heavily depends on QA function. My suggestion is to wait for this function, collaborate with them on agent performance mgmt system, and re-assess the need for competencies development assessment. 
* In the future, we may potentially run an AB test of competencies assessment to see what kind of insights it gives us from onboarding perspective. 
* The final conclusion is that we shouldn’t invest time and effort into developing anything TTP-related for CS Delivery and suppliers given all the dependencies because we don’t want to duplicate efforts. Once the function is in place though, we should closely collaborate.

With regard to termination rights, I am copying here the advice although most of you were cc’d anyway (bold is my addition):

_Regarding the tenant's termination rights: as I pointed out earlier, in the current wording of the agreement Bolt does not have the right to terminate the agreement. According to the Polish Civil Code, a tenant may terminate a lease agreement concluded for a definite term only for the reasons specified in the agreement. The reasons for termination should be specified precisely, whereas the grounds for termination contained in section 10.1.1. of  General Terms are quite general. Therefore, clause 8.12 was added to the agreement, according to which an uninterrupted supply of electricity is necessary for Bolt to be able to use the premises for the intended use of the premises and that interruptions in the supply of electricity for at least 5 consecutive days or for at least 10 days within a 6-month period prevent the tenant from using the premises. We may therefore suggest to the landlord to add in the agreement that in this case (clause 8.12) Bolt is entitled to terminate the agreement immediately. As for other possible grounds for tenant termination, I believe these should be determined by Bolt’s staff who will be using the premises because they will be able to determine under what circumstances the premises may no longer be useful to Bolt._

_Notwithstanding the foregoing,_ *_during the call we did not indicate to the landlord the need to include in the agreement Bolt’s right to terminate the contract._* _In addition to the above, it is the landlord's intention that the agreement continue for the entire term specified in the contract._ *_Therefore, I suggest that the Bolt’s team decide whether Bolt would be willing to enter into the agreement if the landlord does not agree to include in the contract Bolt’s termination right._*

I am not sure why this was not raised on the call - as the lack of termination rights was flagged by me a while back. We need to therefore consider if we can proceed without termination rights or whether we want to push for 8.12 to be a termination right and/or any others (and if so, we need to clearly specify what these should be).

thank you, in accordance with our global approach, in such cases we usually ask the police to provide:

* if possible -  general description of reasoning of why information is requested, and how it pertains to investigation of the alleged crime - this is necessary for us to assess whether scope of requested data is proportionate and we won’t be disclosing more information that is needed for the purpose as prescribed under GDPR
* reference to applicable legal basis (e.g domestic Penal code) under which the police is making this specific request for the information, in particular if the purpose of the disclosure is confidential and we cannot assess the proportionality of the request.

In such instances we usually send on the response as follows:

_Dear Sir/Madam,_

_while we are more than willing to cooperate with the Police, we kindly ask you to supplement formal request with legal basis and the general purpose of requested data disclosure._

_Bolt recognises the legitimate interests in making necessary and proportionate disclosures to the police and law enforcement agencies in order for the authorities to undertake statutory law enforcement functions. Indeed, Bolt usually relies on the legitimate interest lawful basis in order to facilitate such disclosures. For legitimate interests to prevail, and to satisfy the condition, Bolt must undertake the associated assessment, including assessing proportionality of the request and legal basis of the inquiry._ 

_Once we receive information on legal basis and the general purpose of the data disclosure, we will make every effort to accommodate your request._
